questions.explanation: True — minerals are inorganic and normally crystalline.

questions.prompt: The three types of mineral resources are metallic, non-metallic and energy.
questions.explanation: True — those are the three types of mineral resources.

questions.prompt: Coal is an energy mineral (fossil fuel).
questions.explanation: True — coal is an energy mineral, a fossil fuel.

questions.prompt: Iron is a non-metallic mineral.
questions.explanation: False — iron is a metallic mineral.

questions.prompt: Limestone is a non-metallic mineral.
questions.explanation: True — limestone is a non-metallic mineral.

questions.prompt: Bauxite is used to make aluminium.
questions.explanation: True — bauxite is processed to make aluminium.

questions.prompt: Energy minerals are renewable and can be replaced quickly.
questions.explanation: False — energy minerals are non-renewable and cannot be replaced in a human lifetime.

questions.prompt: Lustre is the shiny appearance of a metallic mineral.
questions.explanation: True — lustre is a mineral's shiny, reflective appearance.

questions.prompt: About 70% of the Earth's surface is covered with water.
questions.explanation: True — about 70% of Earth's surface is water.

questions.prompt: Seas and oceans hold 95% of all the water on Earth.
questions.explanation: True — 95% of Earth's water is in seas and oceans.

questions.prompt: There are only three oceans in the world.
questions.explanation: False — there are five oceans.

questions.prompt: Oceans are larger and deeper than seas.
questions.explanation: True — oceans are larger and deeper than seas.

questions.prompt: Seas are larger and deeper than oceans.
questions.explanation: False — oceans are larger and deeper than seas.

questions.prompt: The Caspian Sea is enclosed by land on all sides.
questions.explanation: True — the Caspian Sea is the only sea enclosed by land on all sides.

questions.prompt: There are about fifty seas in the world.
questions.explanation: True — there are around fifty seas.

questions.prompt: The remaining 5% of Earth's water is saltwater.
questions.explanation: False — the remaining 5% is freshwater in glaciers, rivers, lakes and underground.

questions.prompt: Most seas are partially enclosed by land.
questions.explanation: True — most seas are partially enclosed by land, except the Caspian.

questions.prompt: The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean in the world.
questions.explanation: True — the Pacific is the largest ocean.

questions.prompt: The Arctic Ocean is the largest ocean.
questions.explanation: False — the Arctic is the smallest ocean.

questions.prompt: The Arctic Ocean is the smallest and shallowest ocean.
questions.explanation: True — the Arctic is the smallest and shallowest.

questions.prompt: The Mariana Trench is the deepest known point on Earth.
questions.explanation: True — the Mariana Trench (10,924 m) is the deepest point on Earth.

questions.prompt: The Mariana Trench is in the Atlantic Ocean.
questions.explanation: False — the Mariana Trench is in the Pacific Ocean.

questions.prompt: The Southern Ocean is also known as the Antarctic Ocean.
questions.explanation: True — the Southern Ocean is also called the Antarctic Ocean.

questions.prompt: The Atlantic Ocean is the second largest ocean.
questions.explanation: True — the Atlantic is the second largest.

questions.prompt: The Puerto Rico Trench is the deepest part of the Atlantic Ocean.
questions.explanation: True — the Puerto Rico Trench (8,600 m) is the Atlantic's deepest part.

questions.prompt: The Java Trench is the deepest part of the Indian Ocean.
questions.explanation: True — the Java Trench (7,258 m) is the Indian Ocean's deepest part.

questions.prompt: The Indian Ocean is the smallest ocean.
questions.explanation: False — the Indian Ocean is the third largest; the Arctic is smallest.

questions.prompt: There are about 25,000 islands in the Pacific Ocean.
questions.explanation: True — the Pacific has about 25,000 islands.

questions.prompt: The Pacific Ocean has the greatest average depth.
questions.explanation: True — the Pacific is the deepest on average (~4,000 m).

questions.prompt: The Fram Basin is the deepest point of the Arctic Ocean.
questions.explanation: True — the Fram Basin (5,665 m) is the Arctic's deepest point.

questions.prompt: The beginning of a river is called its mouth.
questions.explanation: False — the beginning is the source; the mouth is the end.

questions.prompt: A tributary is a smaller stream that flows into a larger river.
questions.explanation: True — a tributary adds its water to a larger river.

questions.prompt: A river system is also called a drainage basin.
questions.explanation: True — a river system is also called a drainage basin or watershed.

questions.prompt: A delta is formed at the source of a river.
questions.explanation: False — a delta forms at the mouth, where sediment is deposited.

questions.prompt: The River Indus empties into the Arabian Sea.
questions.explanation: True — the Indus ends in a delta and empties into the Arabian Sea.

questions.prompt: The Panjnad River is formed by the confluence of five rivers.
questions.explanation: True — Chenab, Jhelum, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej form the Panjnad.

questions.prompt: A meander is a straight section of a river.
questions.explanation: False — a meander is a looping bend in a river.

questions.prompt: A river's current is strongest near its source.
questions.explanation: True — the current is strongest near the source, where the slope is steepest.

questions.prompt: Brackish water is saltier than seawater.
questions.explanation: False — brackish water is less salty than seawater; it is a mix of fresh and salt water.

questions.prompt: The energy of a flowing river comes from gravity.
questions.explanation: True — gravity provides the energy for a river to flow.

questions.prompt: The point where two rivers meet is called a confluence.
questions.explanation: True — a confluence is where two rivers join.

questions.prompt: The hydrological cycle is also known as the water cycle.
questions.explanation: True — hydrological cycle and water cycle are the same thing.

questions.prompt: Solar radiation causes water to evaporate.
questions.explanation: True — the Sun's energy drives evaporation.

questions.prompt: Transpiration is water released by animals through their skin.
questions.explanation: False — transpiration is water released by plants through their leaves.

questions.prompt: Condensation is water vapour cooling and turning into liquid.
questions.explanation: True — condensation turns vapour back into liquid to form clouds.

questions.prompt: Precipitation can fall as rain, snow or hail.
questions.explanation: True — precipitation includes rain, snow, hail, sleet and drizzle.

questions.prompt: An aquifer is a layer of rock saturated with groundwater.
questions.explanation: True — an aquifer is porous rock saturated with groundwater.

questions.prompt: Evaporation is the last stage of the water cycle.
questions.explanation: False — evaporation is the first stage of the water cycle.

questions.prompt: The water cycle replenishes Earth's supply of freshwater.
questions.explanation: True — the water cycle continuously refills freshwater for living things.

questions.prompt: Oceans produce over 50% of the world's oxygen.
questions.explanation: True — oceans produce over half of Earth's oxygen.

questions.prompt: Marine phytoplankton produces about 50% of Earth's oxygen.
questions.explanation: True — phytoplankton produces about half of Earth's oxygen.

questions.prompt: Oceans store 50 times more carbon dioxide than the atmosphere.
questions.explanation: True — oceans store about 50 times more CO₂ than the atmosphere.

questions.prompt: Oceans have no effect on the world's climate.
questions.explanation: False — oceans regulate climate by transporting heat around the globe.

questions.prompt: Some medicines are made from ocean-derived compounds.
questions.explanation: True — ocean compounds help fight cancer, arthritis, Alzheimer's and heart disease.

questions.prompt: Algae are marine plants rich in proteins and nutrients.
questions.explanation: True — algae are nutrient-rich marine plants used as food.

questions.prompt: Phytoplankton is the base of the marine food chain.
questions.explanation: True — phytoplankton is the base of the marine food chain.

questions.prompt: Upwelling brings nutrient-rich deep water to the surface.
questions.explanation: True — upwelling raises nutrient-rich deep water, feeding phytoplankton.

questions.prompt: Major fishing grounds are found in the middle of oceans.
questions.explanation: False — major fishing grounds are along continental coasts in cooler waters.

questions.prompt: About 500,000 marine species are currently known.
questions.explanation: True — around 500,000 marine species are known.

questions.prompt: Blue carbon is carbon stored by oceans and coastal ecosystems.
questions.explanation: True — blue carbon is captured by oceans and coastal plants like mangroves.

questions.prompt: Scientists estimate up to 10 million marine species may exist.
questions.explanation: True — the estimated total is as high as 10 million species.

questions.prompt: Biological hotspots have very few species.
questions.explanation: False — hotspots have an unusually high concentration of rare species.

questions.prompt: Pakistan depends on the Arabian Sea for 95% of its total trade.
questions.explanation: True — 95% of Pakistan's total trade depends on the Arabian Sea.

questions.prompt: Pakistan depends on the Arabian Sea for 100% of its petroleum and oil.
questions.explanation: True — 100% of Pakistan's petroleum, lubricants and oil come via the Arabian Sea.

questions.prompt: CPEC stands for China Pakistan Economic Corridor.
questions.explanation: True — CPEC is the China Pakistan Economic Corridor.

questions.prompt: The Arabian Sea lies to the north of Pakistan.
questions.explanation: False — the Arabian Sea lies to the south of Pakistan.

questions.prompt: Horizontal movements of ocean water are called currents.
questions.explanation: True — horizontal movements are currents; vertical are upwelling/downwelling.

questions.prompt: The Coriolis Effect is caused by the Earth's rotation.
questions.explanation: True — the Coriolis Effect is the bending of fluids due to Earth's rotation.

questions.prompt: In the Northern Hemisphere, fluids bend to the left.
questions.explanation: False — in the Northern Hemisphere fluids bend to the right.

questions.prompt: Gyres are large circular patterns of ocean currents.
questions.explanation: True — gyres are large circular current patterns.

questions.prompt: Wind is a primary force that drives ocean currents.
questions.explanation: True — wind, solar heat, gravity and the Coriolis Effect are primary forces.

questions.prompt: Temperature and density are primary forces of ocean currents.
questions.explanation: False — temperature and density are secondary forces.

questions.prompt: Denser, colder, saltier water tends to sink.
questions.explanation: True — denser water sinks while less dense water rises.

questions.prompt: Upwelling is when surface water sinks into the deep ocean.
questions.explanation: False — that is downwelling; upwelling is deep water rising to the surface.

questions.prompt: Ocean currents move heat from the equator towards the poles.
questions.explanation: True — currents moderate climate by moving heat poleward.

questions.prompt: An island is completely surrounded by water on all sides.
questions.explanation: True — an island is surrounded by water on all sides.

questions.prompt: A peninsula is completely surrounded by water on all sides.
questions.explanation: False — a peninsula is surrounded by water on three sides only.

questions.prompt: Greenland is an example of a continental island.
questions.explanation: True — Greenland is a continental island.

questions.prompt: Hawaii is an example of an oceanic island.
questions.explanation: True — Hawaii is an oceanic island formed by volcanic activity.

questions.prompt: The Bay of Bengal is the largest bay in the world.
questions.explanation: True — the Bay of Bengal is the largest bay.

questions.prompt: The Gulf of Mexico is the largest gulf in the world.
questions.explanation: True — the Gulf of Mexico is the largest gulf.

questions.prompt: An isthmus is a narrow strip of water.
questions.explanation: False — an isthmus is a narrow strip of land; a strait is a narrow strip of water.

questions.prompt: A strait connects two larger water bodies.
questions.explanation: True — a strait is a narrow strip of water joining two larger water bodies.

questions.prompt: The Suez Canal connects the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea.
questions.explanation: True — the Suez Canal joins the Mediterranean and Red Seas.

questions.prompt: The Strait of Hormuz connects the Persian Gulf with the Arabian Sea.
questions.explanation: True — the Strait of Hormuz joins the Persian Gulf and Arabian Sea.

questions.prompt: A gulf has a wider mouth than a bay.
questions.explanation: False — a gulf has a narrow mouth; a bay has a wider opening.
